text:
mina: Quick question — for the onboarding pipeline: should our bench gating be seqlen-aware by default? I'm worried a single fixed golden (e.g., 512) misses regressions at long and short tails.

aj: +1 for stratified sampling. We should capture 16/64/256/1024 buckets at least. coverage vs cost tradeoff though.

sasha: Also remember KV cache & kv-hit patterns change perf a lot. A model that looks fine at 512 uncached might stall once cache warms. We need a warm/cold distinction in microbench.

ramon: Agree on buckets. Practically: 1) collect real seq-len histogram from shadow traffic, 2) map to 4-6 representative buckets, 3) run bench for each. Cheap way: run short synthetic probe per-bucket for perf, and deep golden for 2-3 critical buckets.

mina: I like that. How do we express pass/fail? Do we require all buckets within delta, or weighted by traffic share?

aj: Weighted makes sense for SLOs. But for admission gates we may want a hard cap for any bucket that represents >X% of traffic. e.g., if bucket >10% traffic, fail if latency regresses >20%.

bench-bot: automated-bench-summary: new-model "opt-13b" — baseline 512 p50 42ms, bucket-1024 p50 78ms (+12% vs baseline), kv-warm delta +8%.

elaine: That bot output is great but we need more context: model config, tokenizer changes, quantization variant. Bench reports should include metadata blob for the ingest record (model_id, quant, compiler, seqlen, batch). Otherwise triage is painful.

ramon: +1. Also include memory footprint and peak gpu alloc for each seqlen. We had regressions caused by allocator fragmentation that only show at 1024.

mina: Ok action items: 1) add seq-len histogram collector to prober (ramon), 2) prober to synthesize 4 buckets and run lightweight latency probe + KV warm/cold (aj + bench-bot), 3) bench report schema to include model metadata + mem/alloc (elaine), 4) gate semantics doc: weighted metric for admission, hard caps for heavy buckets (mina to draft).

aj: One more tradeoff: running per-bucket deep golden for every ingest will blow compute. We should default to lightweight probes and only run full golden when config or major perf-affecting metadata changes (tokenizer, quant, kernel). Could tie to a fingerprint diff heuristic.

mina: Good point. Let's add: deep golden triggered by fingerprint delta >= threshold. ramaon/elaine can propose threshold heuristics.

bench-bot: scheduled: create ticket #ML-boarding-489 with bench report schema template and example.

mina: Thanks everyone. I'll draft the gate semantics and post an RFC follow-up with examples (expected JSON of bench report + pass/fail cases). Please add comments to the doc when I post it. :thumbsup:
